subject: Reserved capacity: proposed safety net & bucket allocation
messages:
From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acme.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity ask — safety net for GPU price moves

Evelyn,

Thanks again for the fast demo last week. ACME is preparing an internal ask for a committed reserved capacity purchase (we're targeting a fairly large slot: ~120 A100-equivalent GPU-months annually). Two procurement questions that drive a lot of internal pushback here:

- We need a clear "price safety net" if the market cost for GPUs swings up mid-term. Can Redwood commit to a cap or a capped indexation approach?
- If we sign a 36-month commitment, can you give a deeper up-front discount and a mechanism to rebalance SKU buckets if our usage shifts?

Attached is a short SOW and our expected monthly profile. We're early in legal review but want to understand commercial flexibility before making a formal buy recommendation.

Attached: ACME_Moas_SOW_v3.pdf

Can we get a pricing sketch and a proposed contract guardrail by EOB Wednesday?

Cheers,
Jordan
Jordan Miles
Head of Procurement, ACME AI
procurement@acme.ai

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acme.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 12:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — safety net for GPU price moves

Jordan —

Appreciate the clarity and the SOW. Pitching a short commercial sketch below so your procurement and finance teams have something to react to. I attached a worked pricing scenarios workbook with SKU allocation examples for your profile.

Key proposal (sketch):
- Term: 36 months (preferred)
- Annual committed GPU-months: 120 (with quarterly reporting and rebalancing window)
- Base discount: 18% off published reserved SKU rates on year 1; step-down schedule if usage materially under-indexes to commitment
- Safety net / index clause: prices may adjust quarterly with a capped upward movement of +6% per 12-month period tied to a GPU market index; Redwood will offer an automatic alternative of swapping to a lower-cost quantized variant if indexation triggers
- Exec credit: for signings > 24 months we can structure a one-time commitment credit that vests over the first 6 months to smooth initial spend

See attached: redwood-pricing-scenarios-evh.xlsx (contains 3 scenarios: conservative, expected, aggressive; also shows discount breakeven and per-token cost deltas with index triggers).

Kimberly — can finance confirm if the +6% annual cap is within our internal risk tolerance for this deal size, or do you want a different collar?

Sean / Aditya — heads-up: ACME may ask for deeper up-front discount if they commit to a strict 36-month irrevocable term. If we move >22% discount, we'll need an approval path.

Jordan — if that sketch looks directionally right I can ask legal to draft a short term sheet with the SKU rebalance window and the proposed index language.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-pricing-scenarios-evh.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity ask — safety net for GPU price moves

Evelyn / team —

Reviewed Evelyn's scenarios. A few notes from finance:

1) Collar: +6% annual cap is acceptable as a starting point, but finance recommends adding a downside protection clause — if realized market power downward pushes Wyzk (market index) by >8% in a 12-month rolling window, ACME gets a one-time credit equal to the difference applied against the following invoice. That keeps us competitive on renewals.

2) Discount bands: we can approve up to 20% base discount for a 36-month term without executive approval if the commit is >100 GPU-months/year and accompanied by a commitment credit structure that phases. Anything >20% needs revenue exec sign-off.

3) Rebalancing: define a quarterly 10% rebalancing window (we'll allow +/-10% movement across SKU buckets without repricing) — outside of that we trigger a true-up at published rates.

If ACME pushes for a deeper discount (they often do), please escalate with a short one-pager showing usage profile and the PAYG delta.

Kimberly Park
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 22:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity ask — safety net for GPU price moves

Team —

I reviewed the proposal and Kimberly's guidance. Approve the commercial guardrails with the following executive exception:

- Approve up to 24% base discount for a 36-month irrevocable commitment, but only if all three of these conditions are met:
  1) ACME signs a minimum 36-month commitment (no early exit) and funds the first two months in advance;
  2) We include the +6% annual cap index clause and the finance downside credit (Kim's point) to protect renewals;
  3) Legal accepts a SKU rebalance window capped at +/-10% quarterly and a mandatory quarterly usage report to trigger rebalances.

If ACME insists on >24% we should require a revenue share feature or escrowed credit to mitigate GPU-price exposure. Evelyn — please request a short justification from ACME for >24% (expected runway, expansion projection) and forward that to me.

Legal / Contracts — once Evelyn confirms ACME's sign intent, work the attached head-of-terms into a short term sheet. I'm okay to rubber stamp the final term sheet if the three conditions above are present.
